headline: Streaming strength offsets weak linear and film results
summary_short: Warner Bros. Discovery's Q2 2026 revenue fell 11% y/y to $8,717M as advertising and content declines outweighed 1% distribution growth; GAAP net income dropped to $149M and Adjusted EBITDA fell 4% to $1,879M, even as Streaming Adjusted EBITDA rose 63% ex-FX.
summary_long: Revenue fell 11% y/y (12% ex-FX) to $8,717M: Distribution grew 1% ex-FX on streaming gains, offset by the HBO Max distribution-deal renewal; Advertising fell 22% ex-FX mainly on the NBA's absence; Content fell 26% ex-FX on a weaker Studios theatrical slate. GAAP net income fell to $149M from $1,580M, including $1.1B of acquisition-amortization, content step-up, and restructuring charges. Adjusted EBITDA fell 4% y/y to $1,879M as 63% ex-FX Streaming growth was offset by declines in Studios and Global Linear Networks. Free cash flow fell to $572M on ~$350M of separation costs. Balance sheet: cash $3,369M, gross debt $33.1B, net leverage 3.4x, after repaying the $15B bridge loan with new Term Loan Bs. No forward guidance was issued.

drivers.explanation: Distribution grew 1% ex-FX on streaming subscriber gains, offset by linear declines and the HBO Max distribution-deal renewal; Advertising fell 22% ex-FX mainly on the NBA's absence; Content fell 26% ex-FX on a weaker Studios theatrical slate.

Net income fell as the prior year included a $2,958M gain on debt extinguishment (only a $75M loss this year); current-quarter income also includes $1.1B of acquisition-related amortization, content fair-value step-up, and restructuring charges.
Streaming Adjusted EBITDA rose 63% ex-FX to $512M, but that growth was more than offset by declines in the Studios and Global Linear Networks segments.
